Day 149 Theorem A: Psi^+(s_mu) = frak s_mu, i.e. Psi is exactly the linear map replacing every Schur function by its factorial-Schur counterpart. Corollary B: P_b = sum_{mu |- 2b, l(mu)<=3} K_{mu'(2^b)} frak s_mu. Theorem C: Psi^+(e_3 f) = E_3 tau(Psi^+ f), so tau is multiplication by e_3. Corollary E: the Psi-recursion is the e_2-Pieri rule with all structure constants 0 or 1. This is what makes Conjecture P sharply posed: the Kostka-weighted sum is E-positive although the individual frak s_mu are NOT (frak s_200 = E_1^2 + 6E_1 - E_2 + 11), so the mechanism is a cancellation between factorial Schur functions.

The floor lemma: for symmetric f, V divides T(fV) and the quotient is symmetric, so Psi(f) = T(fV)/V is a well-defined element of Q[E_1,E_2,E_3] (and Psi(1)=1). Proof: T is S_n-equivariant because the SAME univariate map is applied to every variable; fV is alternating; alternating implies divisible by V with symmetric quotient (factor theorem + UFD). First proved in writing/2026-08-18-M-and-R1-note.md Lemma 0 (2026-08-18) and tersely at proofs/2026-08-22-day125-psi-monomial-progress.md:31, plus a code comment in day131_strategy/route2_operator.py; independently re-proved in full on Day 151 (including the two sub-steps Rick had always asserted -- equivariance, and the symmetry half he had never stated) and verified 196/196 in consistent frames (116 e-monomial/Schur inputs in the two good frames + 80 in the knob matrix), 0 failures, with all 12 mismatched-frame cells and 4 non-symmetric controls failing as predicted. children.reason: COINCIDENCE -- and the identification is REFUTED, not merely unproved. Three independent kills. (1) THE CHECK IS VACUOUS: [h]_q at q=1 is h identically, so her weight at q=1 is (-1)^h h; setting h := m+1 IS the identification rather than a test of it, with a global sign absorbed by hand, so any weight of the form +-(m+1) passes. Zero evidential content. (2) RANGE CONTRADICTION, decisive: every mu in Rick's family has at most 3 rows, so any ribbon inside such a shape spans at most 3 rows and any ribbon-height statistic obeys h <= 2 -- but m+1 must run up to l+1, unbounded in l. Worse in the e = 2 domino bridge Clio herself proposes: there h is in {0,1}, so (-1)^h [h]_q is in {0,-1} FOR EVERY q. Her operator can produce a sign; it cannot produce a multiplicity >= 2. That is exactly the thing a domino involution was already known not to manufacture, and the q-deformation does not fix it. (3) THE FAMILY IS NOT A RIBBON ORBIT: a common lambda would have to satisfy lambda contained in (2l+1, l+1, 0) (the componentwise minimum). Enumerating EVERY such lambda and testing whether mu^(m)/lambda is a ribbon (connected, no 2x2) for all m: for l = 2, 3, 4, 5 there is NO lambda whatsoever that works, and at l = 1 the two surviving lambda give heights [1,0] and [0,0] where [1,2] is required. The two sums cannot be the same sum. TWO FURTHER OBSERVATIONS. Nothing on Rick's side deforms: grep over proofs/, writing/, beta-prime/ and memory/ finds no q-parameter anywhere in the Day 118-131 chain. And the (m+1) does not stand alone -- Day 121 (C1, proved) gives the whole object, bar s*_{mu^(m)}(s) = (-1)^m [ (m+1)(s - (2l+1)) + delta_{m,l} ], whose beta_m = (-1)^{m+1}[(m+1)(2l+1) - delta_{m,l}] depends on l whereas [h]_q depends only on h; there is no q-integer shape available for beta_m and no free parameter to carry one. The (m+1) is the SLOPE of a degree-1 polynomial in the specialisation variable s -- an s-derivative, not a count of anything. Rick's own alpha_mu formula was re-derived independently from its definition, 14/14 exact, so what is refuted is the bridge, not either side of it. Rule 6 v2 firing (~#12). Record as a refuted shape-match, not as an open lead.

Day 150 hypothesis: Conjecture P's E-positivity is the shadow of Kerov/Feray positivity. Kerov character polynomials express the normalised characters Sigma_k in the free cumulants R_j of the transition measure, and Biane's conjecture / Feray's theorem says their coefficients are non-negative integers -- a positivity theorem about a Kostka-adjacent expansion in Lambda^*, proved by counting a different model rather than by a sign-reversing involution, i.e. exactly Conjecture P's shape. Rick's pre-registered tests: T1 (does the 3-variable ring receive the R_j?) then T2 (is P_b R-positive?), with the pre-registered rule 'if truncation destroys the structure the bridge is decorative and the question closes'. Both run on Day 151.
children.reason: T1 FAILS and T2 FAILS: Kerov positivity does not survive Rick's 3-variable truncation. (a)/(b) pass -- R_2..R_8 are nonzero on Lambda_3 with the right filtration degree, and (R_2,R_3,R_4) is a polynomial automorphism of A^3_Q. But (c) integrality fails: the Jacobian is -6, so Z[R_2,R_3,R_4] is a proper subring of Rick's integral Lambda_3 (E_2 and E_3 pick up denominators 2 and 6). (d) free generation dies at R_5, which becomes a mixed-sign non-integral polynomial in R_2,R_3,R_4, so 'the expansion in the R's' -- unique in Lambda^* -- is ill-posed in Lambda_3. (e) is decisive: the truncated Sigma_4..Sigma_7, i.e. the very objects Feray PROVED positive, carry 5/10, 6/14, 10/22 and 12/26 negative coefficients and none is integral. The repaired T2 -- lift to the stable Lambda^*, where the expansion is unique and Feray positivity actually lives -- also fails, for both natural lifts of P_b: b=1 gives 2 negatives out of 3 terms, b=2 5/9 (full) and 5/11 (minimal), b=3 11/20 and 6/13, b=4 20/39 and 28/56; none integral. It fails at the smallest case in closed form, P_1 = s*_{(1,1)} = (R_2^2 - R_2 - R_3)/2. The pipeline is validated, not broken: it reproduces Biane's Sigma_1..Sigma_7 exactly with all coefficients non-negative integers, so it does detect Kerov positivity where it exists. Not circular: the tests test positivity of Kerov's Sigma_k, an external theorem, never Conjecture P itself. Two cheap refinements of P_b that, had they worked, would have made E-positivity manifest term by term.

The S_3-orbit refinement of P_b is not positive: 22 of 35 orbit sums (1/V) sum_{beta in S_3 alpha} prod_i u_i^{(beta_i)} V(u+beta) have negative E-coefficients, so cancellation BETWEEN orbits is essential. And the Pieri operator B is not positive on the E-monomial basis: 12 of 35 monomials of degree <= 4 fail, all with E_3-exponent >= 2, plus E_2^4 and E_2^3 E_3. The factorial Schur basis is the right one.

children.approach: (H1): H = tau(F_P)/F_P ∈ Z[E_1,E_2,E_3][[T]]. Conjecture P implies it and would make it combinatorial. Verified for n<=16 symbolically (T^36 numerically as Conjecture H on Day 146). Day 149 §9 puts it in fully explicit, p-adic-free form: the Hurwitz quotient of sum_b (T^b/b!) sum_mu K_{mu'(2^b)} frak s_{mu+(1^3)} by sum_b (T^b/b!) sum_mu K_{mu'(2^b)} frak s_mu lies in E_3 Z[E][[T]]; both numerator and denominator have coefficients in Z[E] and the whole difficulty is the b!. NOTE: (H1) is NOT needed for b_k = 0 mod 3, which is unconditional -- see bk-mod3.json.

Day 149: H = e^{T B_2}(E_3) / (E_3 e^{T B_2}(1)) where B_k = V^{-1} e_k(hat u) V is the e_k-Pieri operator (hat u_i = u_i S_i) and e_3(hat u) = E_3 tau exactly. So (H1) is precisely the statement that a ratio of two 0/1-combinatorial Pieri flows, started at E_3 and at 1, has integral coefficients, the sole source of denominators being the 1/b! -- equivalently a statement about the commutator of e_2-Pieri with e_3-multiplication, which vanishes in Lambda_3 but not after the Psi-twist. Equivalently again (Theorem 5) the tau-shift is insertion of the single cubic g = 1 + 2(e_1+3)T + (e_1^2+4e_1+e_2)T^2 + (e_1e_2-e_3)T^3 into the umbral bracket, with the bridge H(u) = R(-u-1)^{-1}, R(u) = Phi(u+1)/Phi(u); g-identity verified symbolically to T^7 and the bridge to T^8.

Day 149 Proposition 6, a genuine partial (H1): Phi*V is an integer-valued polynomial in u at every T-degree, and V(u+-1)=V(u), so [T^n]H is l-integral at every E coming from a cubic that splits with distinct roots mod l -- binom(l,3) residue classes. Combined with deg <= n (Theorem 2), Schwartz-Zippel gives [T^n]H ∈ Z_(l)[E_1,E_2,E_3] whenever (l-1)(l-2) > 6nl, in particular for all l >> 6n.
Push Proposition 6 to all primes / all n.
children.reason: Impossible by this method, and the write-up says why precisely (§6.4). Split points see only binom(l,3) residue classes and binom(l,3)/l^3 -> 1/6, so the minimal degree of a polynomial vanishing on them is Theta(l): Proposition 6 is optimal for this route, and each prime therefore controls only finitely many coefficients. At l=2 three integers are never distinct mod 2, so there is no information at all; at l=3 the split locus is the single class E = (0,2,0), giving 3-integrality only on that class, which does not exclude a denominator E_3/3. And one cannot escape to non-split points by base change: binom(x,m) does not map O -> O for O unramified over Z_l (binom(zeta_3,2) = zeta_3(zeta_3-1)/2 is not in Z_2[zeta_3]).

children.approach: Conjecture C: [T^n]F_P is l-integral whenever the cubic is separable mod l. Would have given (H1) immediately, since Zariski density over all F_{l^f} upgrades pointwise integrality to Z_l[E].
children.reason: FALSE. Tested over 14835 (integer E, l) pairs with l not dividing the discriminant: 38108 violations, the first at E = (-22, 6, 24), l = 5, n = 5, where v_5(Psi_5) = 0 < v_5(5!) = 1. So the b! cancellation is genuinely a property of the RATIO H, not of F_P.

children.approach: The second half of Conjecture P -- that the minimum coefficient of [T^n]H is exactly n+1 and is attained at E_1^n -- is untouched and open. Day 150 explained the VALUE but not the MINIMALITY: E_1^n has u-degree n = top degree and no E_3, so it lives entirely in the leading symbol at E_2=E_3=0, where the Narayana identity gives (n+1) N(n+1,n+1) = n+1. Nothing yet rules out a smaller coefficient elsewhere.
